# @helpers4/typescript

> Zero-dependency, tree-shakable TypeScript utility functions. Each of the 18 categories below
> ships as its own npm package (`@helpers4/<category>`); `@helpers4/all` bundles everything as
> peerDependencies (documentation only, no code of its own); `helpers4` bundles everything as
> real dependencies with per-category subpaths — install once, get every category, no follow-up
> peer-dependency install to remember.
> Every function is individually importable, fully typed, has 100% test coverage, and its JSDoc
> `@example` block is smoke-tested — treat those examples as verified-correct usage.

## Conventions

- One function per file: `helpers/<category>/<functionName>.ts`. Import from the package, not
  the file path: `import { chunk } from '@helpers4/array'`.
- If unsure which package to install, or if you need more than one category, install the
  single `helpers4` package instead of guessing at `@helpers4/<category>` names — then import
  `from 'helpers4/<category>'` (e.g. `import { chunk } from 'helpers4/array'`). This is exactly
  equivalent to `@helpers4/array`, just reachable from one dependency instead of many. Note that
  bare `import ... from 'helpers4'` (no subpath) does not resolve — there is no code at the
  package root, only `helpers4/<category>` subpaths.
- No mutation — functions return new values instead of mutating arguments, unless documented
  otherwise.
- `readonly` array/object parameters where the function doesn't mutate.
- `any` is never used in this codebase; APIs use `unknown` or generics instead.
- JSDoc `@example` blocks on every export are runnable, verified documentation — safe to copy.

## Packages

- array — array manipulation, chunking, comparison
- ci — CI/CD workflow status formatting (PR comments, pipeline reports)
- color — color conversion and validation
- commit — Conventional Commits parsing, validation, analysis
- date — date/time utilities, comparison, validation
- function — function composition and wrappers (memoize, retry, debounce, …)
- guard — runtime type guards (`isString`, `isArray`, `isDefined`, …)
- id — unique identifier generation (UUID v7, …)
- markdown — Markdown formatting/escaping
- node — Node.js-specific utilities
- number — numeric operations and formatting
- object — object manipulation, deep comparison, merging, path get/set
- observable — RxJS Observable helpers and operators
- promise — promise utilities: retry, delay, timeout, error handling
- string — string manipulation: capitalize, slugify, camelCase, …
- type — compile-time-only TypeScript utility types (`DeepPartial`, `Maybe`, `Prettify`, …)
- url — URL parsing, manipulation, normalization
- version — semantic version parsing and comparison
